summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: GIFT (Gamete Intra-Fallopian Transfer): unfertilized ovum and sperm are introduced into the Fallopian tube for natural IN-VIVO fertilization (indicated when female cannot produce ova). ICSI (Intra-Cytoplasmic Sperm Injection): single selected sperm is directly injected into the ovum cytoplasm under micromanipulation (indicated for severe male oligospermia). IUI (Intra-Uterine Insemination) / AI: washed, motile sperm is instilled into the uterine cavity.

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
IN-VIVO ART MODALITIES MATRIX
                      
   GIFT (Gamete Intra-Fallopian Transfer)
   ├── Unfertilized Ovum + Sperm transferred into Fallopian Tube.
   └── Indication: Female cannot produce ova, but provides suitable tube/uterine environment.
   
   ICSI (Intra-Cytoplasmic Sperm Injection)
   ├── Single sperm injected directly into Ovum cytoplasm using a micropipette.
   └── Indication: Severe male factor infertility (oligospermia / asthenozoospermia).
   
   IUI (Intra-Uterine Insemination) / AI
   ├── Processed high-motility semen injected directly into Uterine cavity.
   └── Indication: Male partner has low sperm count or inability to inseminate.
conceptBreakdown.content:
### 10.1 Specialized In-Vivo and Micromanipulation ART Modalities

| ART Modality | Full Name | Site of Fertilization | Transfer Location | Primary Clinical Indication |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **GIFT** | Gamete Intra-Fallopian Transfer | **In-Vivo** (Inside Fallopian tube) | Fallopian Tube | Female ovulatory failure with intact, patent Fallopian tubes |
| **ICSI** | Intra-Cytoplasmic Sperm Injection | **In-Vitro** (Laboratory) | Culture dish ➔ Embryo transfer | Severe oligospermia ($<2\text{ million/mL}$), azoospermia, or poor sperm motility |
| **IUI** | Intra-Uterine Insemination | **In-Vivo** (Inside female tract) | Uterine Cavity | Mild oligospermia, cervical hostility, or erectile dysfunction |
| **AI** | Artificial Insemination | **In-Vivo** (Vagina or Uterus) | Female Genital Tract | Male partner inability to inseminate female partner |

### 10.2 Modality Breakdown
1. **GIFT (Gamete Intra-Fallopian Transfer)**:
   - Harvested donor ovum and washed capacitated partner sperm are loaded separated by an air bubble in a catheter and deposited into the ampulla of the recipient's Fallopian tube.
   - Fertilization and subsequent cleavage occur naturally *in-vivo* within the patient's own Fallopian tube.
2. **ICSI (Intra-Cytoplasmic Sperm Injection)**:
   - Under an inverted microscope equipped with micromanipulators, an embryologist immobilizes a single morphologically normal spermatozoon with a glass micropipette and injects it directly across the Zona Pellucida and oolemma into the cytoplasm of a mature Metaphase II oocyte.
   - Bypasses all natural barriers of acrosomal reaction and zona binding.
3. **IUI (Intra-Uterine Insemination)**:
   - Semen collected from husband or healthy donor is washed to remove prostaglandins and seminal plasma, concentrating motile spermatozoa in culture medium, and deposited directly into the uterine fundus during the periovulatory window.

conceptBreakdown.heading: Sperm Washing in IUI
conceptBreakdown.title: Sperm Washing in IUI
conceptBreakdown.content: Unwashed semen cannot be injected into the uterus because high concentrations of seminal prostaglandins induce severe, agonizing uterine cramps and anaphylactoid shock.

conceptBreakdown.heading: TESE / PESA in Azoospermic ICSI
conceptBreakdown.title: TESE / PESA in Azoospermic ICSI
conceptBreakdown.content: In non-obstructive or obstructive azoospermia, viable spermatozoa can be surgically extracted directly from the epididymis (PESA) or testicular tissue biopsy (TESE) for successful ICSI.
